per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window: the 2021 relaxation study of apo, reduced AnaCTDH (35 °C, pH 7.0, 700 MHz; the BMRB-50410 sample) reports ps-ns backbone motion and relates it to the mobile C-terminal tail, but prints no S2 values or residue list (ALL4940-J1, 21-r1).
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window, localized but without a rate: in the same sample the largest Rex and broadened signals sit in the beta5-beta6 loop T101-G105 near the putative dimer interface (ALL4940-J2; 21-r1, 21-r2); other missing amides (M1-A4, T20, F53, A76, L127, L137, R139) are attributed mostly to conformational broadening but stay unresolved (ALL4940-J18). No dispersion, CEST or R1rho is in the evidence, and the dispersion search did not use the alias AnaCTDH/CTDH.
per_window.slower_than_ms: unresolved (search_insufficient): no HDX, time-resolved, multitemperature, FRET or EPR evidence, and the search used only 'All4940 protein' (ALL4940-J3). The cargo-transfer and SEC assays run over seconds to an hour but measure carotenoid movement or apparent size, not protein motion, and are not counted here.
per_window.undetermined: Structure-only and MD evidence of a movable C-terminal tail: the 6S5L apo crystal holds two tail orientations in six chains each, a third position being the closed 6FEJ tail (ALL4940-J7; 21-r3, 21-r4, structure_only); apo MD opens the tail in 2 of 6 runs through a perpendicular intermediate (ALL4940-J8, 21-r6, md_only), a docked holo model also opens in 2 of 6 (J19, 21-r7), L128D stalls at the intermediate (J20, 21-r8) and L137D flips in all three runs (J21, 21-r9). The 2018 apo crystal (urea, disulfide dimer) has an inward, cavity-capping tail compared with the outward tail of homolog holo-OCP (ALL4940-J4; r4, 21-r5) and holds two dimer interfaces in one lattice (ALL4940-J5, r4); both unresolved. Homolog SAXS of Synechocystis CTD shows flexible termini (ALL4940-J6, r5, inference_from_homolog). Not counted in any window (binding kinetics or apparent size, C103F mutants): carotenoid uptake, delivery and SEC assays (2018: ALL4940-J9 to J16, r6-r20; 2020: ALL4940-J22 to J25, 21-r10 to 21-r20). Wild-type holo All4940 has no experimental structure or dynamics evidence (ALL4940-J17).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Partly, without rates: in the apo, reduced wild-type protein at 35 °C, pH 7.0 (700 MHz, the BMRB-50410 sample), 15N relaxation shows ps-ns backbone motion linked to the C-terminal tail and a conformational-exchange (Rex) contribution centred on the beta5-beta6 loop T101-G105, whose S102-G105 amides are broadened beyond detection, next to the putative dimer interface, with no kex, population or minor state reported; crystal (6S5L, 6FEJ) and MD evidence shows a C-terminal tail that takes several positions, also without a rate.
protein_summary.deposition_readback: Deposition-derived; same numbers RelaxDB labels were computed from; not literature confirmation. BMRB 50410 holds one 700 MHz R1/R2/NOE set at 308 K, pH 7.0 for 108 residues, with no data for M1-A4, T20, F53, A76, S102-G105, L127, L137 or R139 (the amides the 2021 paper could not observe); NOE below 0.65 marks A5-K14, A71, Q72, S86, E87, T123 and E133-L135 as fast-moving, and R2/R1 above the 20.8 cut flags E70, G81-A83, A99, H122, I125 and K126, while T101, the one beta5-beta6 loop residue with data, is not flagged. Twelve further assigned residues also have no deposited rates (A29, A40, D46, I63, D88, K98, L109, Q116, A136, R138, E140, Q141).
open_conflicts: Source numbering, not a dynamics conflict: the 2018 paper uses native numbering (C103, W102, Y26; entry = native + 1), the 2021 NMR paper uses 6FEJ numbering equal to the entry (C104, W103, Y27), and the 2020 BBA paper uses entry numbering for residues (L82, L128, L137, W110) but the native label C103F for the entry-C104 mutant; Gln132 in the 2018 paper still maps to entry E133 and stays unmapped, and Asn94 in a 2020 caption conflicts with Q94.
Supplementary Fig. 8F caption names HCP4 while the panel label and main text name HCP1 (r20); HCP1 was used.

Membrane-uptake endpoint for C103F: 100% after 1 h in 2018 (r13) versus 80.30% in 2020 (21-r17) under the same nominal assay (33 °C, 12 µM dimers, 48 µM canthaxanthin); binding endpoint, not a dynamics conflict.
questions_for_gina: The BMRB-50410 sample is apo and reduced and the authors treat it as monomeric, yet tau_c is 10.0 ns at 35 °C for a 16 kDa protein; should the entry be carried as apo monomer, or as an apo monomer/dimer mixture whose R2 (and the R2/R1 flags) may include self-association?
Should the oxidized disulfide-linked apo dimer (crystals) and the reduced apo monomer (NMR) be carried as separate sample states for the wild-type apo answer?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Row-id shorthand: 21-rN = ALL4940-50410_20261017115440-rN; rN alone = ALL4940-rN. The NMR sample is in 40 mM sodium phosphate pH 7.0 with 2.7 mM DTT; no row establishes phosphate binding by AnaCTDH, so no artefact is assigned. The 6S5L crystal grew from 1.26 M NaH2PO4 / 0.14 M K2HPO4 at pH 5 and the 6FEJ crystal with 1 M urea at pH 4.2 after 2 M urea pretreatment, both of which can select tail positions. All carotenoid-transfer and SEC rows (2018 and 2020) use C103F mutants (no covalent disulfide), so they bear on wild type only by inference; the codex second-read could not confirm canthaxanthin as the cargo in the 2018 HCP-donor assays (r6-r12, r15-r20). Apo vs holo and disulfide dimer vs monomer are different sample states: carotenoid binding dimerizes CTDH and apo CTDH tends to monomerize when reduced, and its monomer/dimer ratio is concentration-dependent. The literature search for this entry used only the name 'All4940 protein'; aliases AnaCTDH/CTDH were not searched, so absent method classes are search gaps.
